earlier_scan.source_named: Snell, Rupert. 1991. The Hindi Classical Tradition: A Braj Bhasa Reader (grammar sketch). Grierson 1916 LSI IX-1 (read online) has no Braj stress statement.

sources.citation: Rawat, Chandrabhan. 1967. Mathura jile ki boli [The dialect of Mathura district] (PhD, Agra University, dir. Vishwanath Prasad). Allahabad: Hindustani Academy. archive.org;ernet.dli.2015.493996
sources.note: Closest, but no placement rule. Structuralist phonemics (with A. Kelkar's input): suprasegmental inventory §1.1.3/1.1.31 (c. p.145) = word/clause/sentence junctures, rising/falling/level terminal contours, one non-terminal 'balvarddhak' (sentence emphasis) and contour modifiers; word stress is not in the inventory. 'balaghat-yukt/-rahit' (stressed/unstressed) appears only as allophone conditioning (pp.134-136), incl. p.135 'बलाघात, उपसर्ग पर न होकर, पद पर होता है' (in prefixed words like /niDar/ the stress is on the base, not the prefix); reduced short-vowel allophones occur 'word-medially be…

sources.citation: Ojha, Neetesh Kumar & Shakuntala Mahanta. 2026. Perceptual correlates of lexical tone in Brajbhasha. Speech Prosody 2026, 907-911. doi:10.21437/SpeechProsody.2026-184
sources.note: Tone perception study; 'The syllable is the TBU, and the Low tone so far has been observed to be hosted only by heavy TBUs'; no word-stress statement.

sources.citation: Ojha, Neetesh Kumar & Shakuntala Mahanta. 2023. Vowels, tones, and tonogenesis in Braj. Proc. 2nd International Conference on Tone and Intonation (TAI 2023), Singapore, 73-77. doi:10.21437/TAI.2023-16
sources.note: Instrumental (11 Mathura/Bharatpur speakers): vowel space, length only phonetic, and a Low vs neutral lexical tone from loss of /h/; says nothing about word stress.

tone.says: Not opened (embargoed). From the title and the author's two published chapters (the works listed here): a full first-hand instrumental analysis of Brajbhasha lexical tone - a Low tone contrasting with neutral/default pitch, arising from loss of intervocalic/coda /h/ (tonogenesis), syllable as TBU with Low hosted on heavy syllables, production and perception experiments, plus (per the companion article title) 'tonoexodus', i.e. ongoing loss/erosion of the contrast by generation and education. sources.note: The only full modern reference grammar of spoken Braj (Glottolog's top-ranked description, 'takes account of the dialects of the whole Braj area'); Soviet NIA grammars of this series normally carry a phonetics chapter with an explicit paragraph on ударение. Most likely place for a first-hand placement statement.

sources.note: Journal-length treatment of Brajbhasha lexical tone (Low vs neutral from /h/ loss per the authors' earlier papers), its tonogenesis, and 'tonoexodus' (Ratliff's term for tone loss) - i.e. likely argues the young tone contrast is already eroding in some speaker groups, consistent with the generation/education effects reported in their Speech Prosody 2026 perception paper.
